claim: Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN makes the user experience more consistent by using the highly available and congestion-free AWS global network instead of multiple public internet networks.
question: Why should you use Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN?

values.spoken: traffic uses the AWS global network instead of the congested internet

evidence.quote: VPN connections face inconsistent availability and performance as traffic traverses through multiple public networks on the internet before reaching the VPN endpoint in AWS. These public networks can be congested. Each hop can introduce availability and performance risks. Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN makes user experience more consistent by using the highly available and congestion-free AWS global network.

note: FAQ question: 'Why should I use Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN?' (item 41).

claim: Only a transit gateway supports Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN, so you specify a transit gateway when you create the VPN connection; the AWS-side VPN endpoint is created on the transit gateway.
question: Is Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN supported for both a virtual private gateway and an AWS Transit Gateway?

values.display: Only Transit Gateway supports Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN
values.spoken: only a transit gateway supports accelerated VPN

evidence.quote: Only Transit Gateway supports Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN. A Transit Gateway should be specified when creating a VPN connection. The VPN endpoint on the AWS side is created on the Transit Gateway.

note: FAQ question: 'Is Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN supported for both virtual gateway and AWS Transit Gateway?' (item 45).

claim: You create an Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN by setting the option Enable Acceleration to true when you create the VPN connection.
question: How can you create an Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN?

values.spoken: turn on the Enable Acceleration option

qualifiers.condition: set when creating the VPN connection

evidence.quote: When creating a VPN connection, set the option “Enable Acceleration” to ‘true’.

note: FAQ question: 'How can I create an Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN?' (item 42).

claim: To convert an existing Site-to-Site VPN to an Accelerated one you create a new accelerated VPN, point your customer gateway device at it, and delete the old connection; you get new tunnel endpoint IP addresses because accelerated VPNs use separate IP address ranges.
question: How can you convert an existing Site-to-Site VPN to an Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN?

values.display: Create a new Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN
values.spoken: create a new accelerated VPN and delete the old one

evidence.quote: Create a new Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN, update your customer gateway device to connect to this new VPN connection, and then delete your existing VPN connection. You will get new tunnel endpoint internet protocol (IP) addresses since accelerated VPNs use separate IP address ranges from non-accelerated VPN connections.

note: FAQ question: 'How can I convert my existing Site-to-Site VPN to an Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN?' (item 44).

claim: Each Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connection offers two tunnels for high availability.
question: Does an Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connection offer two tunnels for high availability?

evidence.quote: Yes, each VPN connection offers two tunnels for high availability.

note: FAQ question: 'Does an Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connection offer two tunnels for high availability?' (item 46).

claim: NAT-T is required and enabled by default for Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connections.
question: Is NAT-T required for Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connections?

values.display: NAT-T is required and is enabled by default
values.spoken: NAT-T is required and on by default

evidence.quote: NAT-T is required and is enabled by default for Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connections.

note: FAQ question: 'Are there any protocol differences between Accelerated and non-Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN tunnels?' (item 47).

claim: Apart from NAT-T, accelerated and non-accelerated VPN tunnels support the same IPsec and IKE protocols and offer the same bandwidth, tunnel options, routing options, and authentication types.
question: Besides NAT-T, are there protocol differences between accelerated and non-accelerated Site-to-Site VPN tunnels?

values.display: offer the same bandwidth, tunnel options, routing options
values.spoken: same bandwidth, options and routing as a normal VPN

evidence.quote: Other that that, Accelerated and non-Accelerated VPN tunnels support the same IP security (IPSec) and internet key exchange (IKE) protocols, and also offer the same bandwidth, tunnel options, routing options, and authentication types.

note: FAQ question: item 47. The page prints 'Other that that'.

claim: Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN can only be created through AWS Site-to-Site VPN, and it cannot be created through the AWS Global Accelerator console or API.
question: Is Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN an option in AWS Global Accelerator?

values.display: cannot be created through the AWS Global Accelerator console or API
values.spoken: you cannot create it in the Global Accelerator console

evidence.quote: No, Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN can only by created through AWS Site-to-Site VPN. Accelerated Site-to-Site VPNs cannot be created through the AWS Global Accelerator console or API.

note: FAQ question: 'Is Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN an option in AWS Global Accelerator?' (item 49). The page prints 'can only by created'.

claim: Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN over public Direct Connect virtual interfaces is not available; in most cases it would give no acceleration benefit there.
question: Can you use Accelerated VPN over public AWS Direct Connect virtual interfaces?

values.display: over public Direct Connect virtual interfaces is not available
values.spoken: accelerated VPN does not run over a public virtual interface

evidence.quote: No, Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN over public Direct Connect virtual interfaces is not available. In most cases there is no acceleration benefit of Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN when used over public Direct Connect.

note: FAQ question: 'Can I use Accelerated VPN over public AWS Direct Connect virtual interfaces?' (item 50).

claim: Enabling Site-to-Site VPN logs on an existing connection through the modify tunnel options interrupts connectivity over the tunnel for up to several minutes; enable logging one tunnel at a time so only the modified tunnel is impacted.
question: What happens when you enable Site-to-Site VPN logs on an existing VPN connection?

values.display: interrupted for up to several minutes
values.spoken: the tunnel is interrupted for a few minutes

qualifiers.condition: logs enabled on an existing connection with the modify tunnel options

evidence.quote: When you enable Site-to-Site VPN logs to an existing VPN connection using the modify tunnel options, your connectivity over the tunnel is interrupted for up to several minutes. Each VPN connection offers two tunnels for high availability. You can enable logging on one tunnel at a time and only the modified tunnel will be impacted.

note: FAQ question: 'What happens when I enable Site-to-Site VPN logs to my existing VPN connection?' (item 55).

claim: You can choose any private ASN for the Amazon side of the BGP session: 16-bit private ASNs from 64512 to 65534, or 32-bit ASNs between 4200000000 and 4294967294.
question: Which ASN can you choose for the Amazon side of a virtual private gateway BGP session?

evidence.quote: You can choose any private ASN. Ranges for 16-bit private ASNs include 64512 to 65534. You can also provide 32-bit ASNs between 4200000000 and 4294967294.

note: FAQ question: 'What ASN can I choose?' (item 100).

claim: Amazon does not validate ownership of ASNs, so the Amazon-side ASN is limited to private ASNs, to protect customers from BGP spoofing.
question: Why can you not assign a public ASN for the Amazon half of the BGP session?

values.spoken: private ASNs only, to prevent BGP spoofing

evidence.quote: Amazon is not validating ownership of the ASNs, therefore, we’re limiting the Amazon-side ASN to private ASNs. We want to protect customers from BGP spoofing.

note: FAQ question: 'Why can’t I assign a public ASN for the Amazon half of the BGP session?' (item 99).

claim: You cannot modify the Amazon side ASN of a virtual private gateway after creation; you delete the virtual gateway and recreate it with the desired ASN.
question: Can you change the Amazon side ASN once the virtual gateway is created?

values.display: you cannot modify the Amazon side ASN after creation
values.spoken: the Amazon side ASN cannot be changed after creation

evidence.quote: No, you cannot modify the Amazon side ASN after creation. You can delete the virtual gateway and recreate a new virtual gateway with the desired ASN.

claim: The VPN FAQ says a private ASN in the range 4200000000 to 4294967294 is not currently supported for a customer gateway configuration.
question: Is a 32-bit private-range ASN supported for a customer gateway?

qualifiers.condition: private ASN in the range 4200000000 to 4294967294

evidence.quote: Please note, private ASN in the range of (4200000000 to 4294967294) is NOT currently supported for Customer Gateway configuration.

note: FAQ question: 'I want to use 32-bit ASN for my Customer Gateway. Is 32-bit private range ASN supported?' (item 119). The Direct Connect document history lists 4-byte ASN support from 2025-09; compare with the user guide before use.

claim: Amazon provides an ASN for the virtual gateway if you do not choose one: after June 30th 2018 that ASN is 64512 (until then it was the legacy public ASN of the Region).
question: Which ASN does Amazon assign to a virtual private gateway if you do not choose one?

qualifiers.condition: no ASN provided at creation; behavior stated for after June 30th 2018

evidence.quote: Amazon will provide an ASN for the virtual gateway if you don’t choose one. Until June 30th 2018, Amazon will continue to provide the “legacy public ASN” of the region. After June 30th 2018, Amazon will provide an ASN of 64512.

note: FAQ question: 'If I don’t provide an ASN for the Amazon half of the BGP session, what ASN can I expect Amazon to assign to me?' (item 102).
